problem_statement: devmamunur/Babsa-Business-And-Agency-HTML-Template, rebranded here as Northwind Freight Systems (a freight-logistics dispatch and shipment-analytics platform), is a static Bootstrap marketing site served from index.html plus local css/, js/, images/, font/, and fonts/ (no build step). The site now spans a scroll-anchored home page (index.html) and two secondary pages, pricing.html and contact.html, that share the same top navigation. Deliver a coordinated 'freight coverage' feature while preserving the Bootstrap shell, the nav anchors, the scripts and the responsive behavior: (1) Add a 'Freight coverage' section (#coverage) to the home page just above the pricing table, with a metric strip of four tiles (Lanes tracked / Carrier connections / On-time delivery / Regions served). REPAIR its responsive layout so the strip stays within the viewport on a 390px phone with no horizontal overflow — do not merely clip it with overflow-x:hidden; the document itself must not exceed the mobile viewport width. (2) Promote the freight-lane taxonomy into a shared 'Freight lanes covered' rail (Regional / Long-haul / Intermodal lane chips) that appears CONSISTENTLY on the home coverage section AND on the pricing.html AND contact.html pages, styled to match the Northwind ivory/blue palette (light surface, restrained blue border, rounded chips) — the rendered rail must be visually faithful to the reference, not a collapsed or off-palette slab. (3) Wire the coverage lane filter end to end: clicking a lane filter button (Regional lane / Long-haul lane / Intermodal lane) must update the '#coverage-readout' readout to 'Showing: <selected lane>' in addition to highlighting the active button — the post-click terminal state must reflect the selected lane, not the default 'Showing: All lanes'. Keep the hero, services grid, works gallery, testimonials, pricing table, team, counters, contact block, footer, scripts, and desktop/tablet layout intact, and keep the site static with a clean browser console (no remote CDN/font/map requests).
required_content: A 'Freight coverage' section (#coverage) is added to the home page above the pricing table with four metric tiles (Lanes tracked / Carrier connections / On-time delivery / Regions served) that render within the viewport on a 390px phone with no horizontal document overflow beyond 24px.

A shared 'Freight lanes covered' rail (Regional / Long-haul / Intermodal lane chips) appears CONSISTENTLY on the home coverage section AND on the pricing.html AND contact.html pages — the same lane component in all three places, not only on the home page.

The 'Freight lanes covered' rail and the coverage strip keep the Northwind ivory/blue palette (light surface, restrained blue border, rounded chips) and are visually faithful to the reference rendering — not a collapsed or off-palette restyle.

The coverage lane filter is wired end to end: clicking a lane filter button updates the '#coverage-readout' readout to 'Showing: <selected lane>' (e.g. clicking Regional lane sets 'Showing: Regional lane') in addition to marking the button active; the post-click terminal state reflects the selected lane, not the default 'Showing: All lanes'.

The pricing.html and contact.html secondary pages share the home navigation and remain reachable (real routes, not 404), and the desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts stay within their viewports.

The hero, services grid, works gallery, testimonials, pricing table, team, counters, contact block, and footer remain reachable and unchanged, and the static site keeps a clean browser console (no remote CDN/font/map errors).
design_constraints: Fix the responsive layout of the Freight coverage metric strip; do not delete the strip, change its four tiles, or restyle unrelated sections.

Add the SAME shared 'Freight lanes covered' rail component to the home coverage section, the pricing.html page AND the contact.html page so the lane language is consistent site-wide; do not add it to only one page.
Preserve the Northwind/Bootstrap design language: existing section rhythm, nav anchors, ivory/blue accent, rounded cards; the rail must render in the ivory/blue editorial palette.
Keep the lane filter interaction wired end to end (the #coverage-readout terminal readout must reflect the clicked lane), not merely a class toggle.

Do not introduce external stylesheets, remote fonts, CDNs, or new remote script/asset dependencies; the site must stay a self-contained static build with a clean console, and the secondary pages must share the same nav and stay real routes.
state_constraints: The home states (desktop, mobile, tablet) capture the scrolled-to-top hero; the rebrand must land the Northwind headline and brand above the fold on desktop_home.

The section states scroll to their anchors: desktop_services and mobile_services to #servicepart, desktop_pricing to #pricing, desktop_team to #team, and desktop_contact to #contactuspart, so each rewritten section is captured in place.

change_completion: The Freight coverage metric strip renders its four tiles within the viewport on mobile.
The shared 'Freight lanes covered' rail appears on the home coverage section, the pricing.html page AND the contact.html page.
The lane filter click updates the #coverage-readout terminal readout to the selected lane.
design_consistency: The Northwind palette, section rhythm, accent color, and nav are preserved.
The 'Freight lanes covered' rail keeps the ivory/blue editorial look and is visually faithful to the reference across the home + secondary pages.
interaction_continuity: Clicking a lane filter button updates the 'Showing:' readout to the selected lane (post-click terminal state reflects the change, not the default).
regression: Hero, services, works, testimonials, pricing, team, counters, contact and footer remain reachable and unchanged.
The static site serves from index.html + pricing.html + contact.html with a clean console.
responsive: 390px home (initial, coverage) and the mobile pricing page have no horizontal overflow beyond 24px; 834px tablet is clean.
The metric tiles wrap or shrink cleanly instead of forcing a fixed-width row.

author_notes: Repo-grounded static multi-page marketing task (Babsa rebranded as Northwind Freight Systems) hardened to L4. The reference (a) adds a Freight coverage section with a metric strip that WRAPS fluidly on mobile (flex 1 1 150px -> 0 overflow), (b) promotes a shared 'Freight lanes covered' rail into the home coverage section AND the pricing.html AND contact.html pages in the Northwind ivory/blue palette, and (c) wires the coverage lane filter so #coverage-readout reflects the clicked lane. The baseline is the original layout defect: a fixed 760px nowrap strip (overflows mobile ~385px), NO rail anywhere (D2 fails on all three pages, D3 fails) but the lane-filter JS is CORRECT (baseline PASSES D4 -> leg-orthogonal). The bad 'smart-wrong' solution narrows the strip to 560px + overflow-x:hidden on the strip (still overflows document ~185px -> D6 fail), adds the rail to the HOME page only (D2 cross-page fail on pricing + contact), restyles the rail into a collapsed dark-teal slab (D3 visual_regression fail: block color_delta_e ~62, ssim ~0.59), and toggles the filter's .active class without re-syncing #coverage-readout (click succeeds but the readout stays 'Showing: All lanes' -> D4 interaction_assertions fail). bad fails FOUR distinct gates while all text/completion/regression/console signals pass. The secondary pages load the same plugin script set as the home page so the shared script.js runs pageerror-free on all legs (declared INFRA, identical across the three legs).

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Static single-page Bootstrap agency marketing template (Babsa) with generic demo copy across hero, services, pricing, team, and contact sections; an ideal host for a state_continuity modify task that rebrands the whole page into a Northwind Freight Systems freight-logistics platform while preserving the Bootstrap shell, nav anchors, and responsive layout.
